verdict.explanation: The reconstructed proposal says “Last updated: September 1, 2026,” but its metadata says September 26, 2026. It also unconditionally tells consumers they may submit requests through the email address and web path, although both are synthetic fixtures and their usability is unverified. Finally, the provider-disclosure list does not say which categories were disclosed for a business purpose in the preceding 12 months, as required by Civil Code §1798.130(a)(5)(C)(ii). The other changed clauses are related to the California signup and its disclosure obligations; no unrelated-clause modification was identified. This review concerns an unapproved proposal, not publication or operational compliance.
operational_requirements: Founder: assess whether collecting a full postal address is necessary and proportionate; change the signup fields only through a separately approved factual/product decision.

Founder: confirm a monitored request email, usable web form, identity and agent handling, and trained request operations before claiming the channels work or publishing them.
Founder: authorize publication separately, only after operational facts match the policy.
Lawyer: verify processor contracts, no sale or sharing, retention, credential practices, absence of significant-decision ADMT, and reporting thresholds before real-world reuse.
